C0 explicitly preserves omitted-control ABI-1 compatibility.

findings.detail: The three merged expectations pass only after F1 changes the submitted bodies. The original source does not establish new v2 landings; it establishes ABI-1 native semantic requests. Therefore the change cannot distinguish genuine new-v2 merged receipts from historical ABI-1 rebased behavior.
findings.required_first_return: Keep genuine new-v2 merged coverage separate. Restore these original node inputs and retain rebased unless a source-approved migration changes the caller itself and preserves the original behavior purpose.

findings.detail: The guarded registered-provider doc.patch setup deep-copies the current empty parent payload and asserts payload equality, which is source-consistent with the old empty topology. It does not by itself prove source capture, original pin retention, dynamic-base behavior, real HTTP lost-ACK, restart, or undo. The central HTTP route failed before collection, so no body credit is assigned.
findings.required_first_return: After resolving F1/F2, run the exact HTTP node through the qualified central route with the required immutable Runtime/provider prerequisites; do not use a fixture workaround or a second body.

findings.detail: The retired setup authored config={tracks: []}, registry={}, clips=[], occurrences=[]; the current bootstrap baseline is config={clips: [], tracks: []}, registry={}, clips=[], occurrences=[]. Frozen R4 _complete_parent_payload defaults config to {} and does not synthesize config.clips. The replacement therefore changes the parent payload topology by adding config.clips, even though its self-equality assertion proves only equality to the changed baseline.
findings.required_first_return: Construct the replacement from an existing registered commitTimeline/provider caller while preserving the old authored parent payload exactly, including omission of config.clips, or obtain explicit approval for that authored topology change.
